_comment: P94 claim-proof binding (drift invariant 60, tools/sync_check.py::check_claim_proof). A universal claim about this repo's own behavior is a promise, and a promise ships with the executed proof that keeps it. `claims` bind a verbatim sentence to either an enforced drift invariant (`invariant:N`) or a NAMED selftest pin the battery actually runs (`tools/x.py::selftest::<label substring>`). `exempt` records a universal that no code can prove -- a standing instruction to the agent -- with a written reason. `routes` bind an install route the docs RECOMMEND to the code that must DETECT it. `corpus` is the guarded set: a universal claim there that appears in none of the three lists fails the build.
_why: Documentation truth checks paths, symbols, counts, URLs and hashes, and a universal sentence names none of those, so no token check can see it; this manifest ties each such sentence to an executed proof or a written exemption.

claims.claim: Each `::selftest::` proof also names, in the manifest's `boundaries`, the CLI entry, tool or runtime default its claim describes, and invariant 60 fails when no live code in the pin's function calls that entry and the record states no gap naming it
claims.why: check_claim_proof runs _claim_boundary_problems over every `::selftest::` proof the claims use: a proof with no boundaries record, a boundary name its module does not define, and a pin whose function never calls its boundary while the record states no gap of 25 characters naming it each fail. _claim_boundary_self_proof shows those refusals on a fixture first, and _CLAIM_WIRING fails the build when the call is removed.

claims.claim: runs with no model tokens: outside its selftests, the code it runs imports only the standard library plus `registry_io` and `atomic_io`, starts no process, sends requests only to `pypi.org` and `api.github.com`, and reads one credential from the environment, a GitHub token
claims.proof: tools/dependency_currency.py::selftest::token-free: outside its selftests the import closure
claims.why: The selftest reads the import closure of dependency_currency.py statically, skipping the functions named selftest and _selftest. It fails on a module outside the standard library other than registry_io and atomic_io, on a refused standard-library module (subprocess, multiprocessing, concurrent, importlib, runpy, ctypes, pty, webbrowser, asyncio, pkgutil, zipimport, builtins, code, codeop, pickle, marshal, shelve, _posixsubprocess, socket, socketserver, http, ftplib, smtplib, imaplib, poplib, nntplib, telnetlib, xmlrpc), on a process-spawning or dynamic-code call, on a network call outside _http_get_json, on an environment read other than REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN, and when _ALLOWED_HOSTS is anything but pypi.org and api.github.com. It also hands _http_get_json a recording opener: a URL on another host is refused before anything is sent, and a redirect to another host is refused. It reads code, not traffic: a credential read from a file is not seen. A model request needs a model host, which the host check refuses, or a process or model client, which the closure check refuses; the conclusion rests on pypi.org and api.github.com serving no model inference.

_boundaries_why: Pin-boundary records (docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md section 7.3). A claim describes what a person reaches through a CLI entry, a tool or a runtime default; each `::selftest::` proof the claims use names that entry here as `tools/x.py::name` or `tools/x.py::Class.method`. Invariant 60 fails on a proof with no record, a name the module does not define, and a pin whose function never calls its entry while the record states no `gap` of at least 25 characters naming it. A `gap` is a recorded limit: move the pin to the entry or narrow the claim.

boundaries.gap: The pin reads the module's source statically (_import_closure over its own file, main and what it calls included) rather than running main.

routes.why: uv installs itself and `uv python install`'s pythonX.Y into ~/.local/bin (uv docs, Installing Python). P93 recommended this route while env_paths searched only the Homebrew prefixes and the launcher probed only machine-wide paths, so the Python its own message told the user to install was invisible.

nvm keeps each node under $NVM_DIR/versions/node/<version>/bin (nvm.sh::nvm_version_path) and is sourced per shell. P93 made nvm the recommended Node route while env_paths could not see it, so the wizard looped users on 'Still not detecting Node.js 20 or higher' after issuing its own nvm command.

guarded_text.mirror_of: Every change that removes text or files from a guard's scan set ships a committed case for the removed set

guarded_text.text: **The manifest names the boundary.** Every `::selftest::` proof in `tools/claim-proof-manifest.json` has a `boundaries` record naming that entry as `tools/x.py::name` or `tools/x.py::Class.method`.
guarded_text.why: A section 7.3 rule of docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md, outside the guarded corpus; deleting it fails invariant 60.

guarded_text.text: **What the boundary check does not see.** It reads calls by name.
guarded_text.why: A section 7.3 rule of docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md, outside the guarded corpus; deleting it fails invariant 60.

guarded_text.text: Each selftest proof names the entry its claim describes in the manifest's `boundaries`, and invariant 60 fails when the pin does not call it and no gap naming it is recorded (7.3).
guarded_text.why: The AGENTS.md restatement of a CLAUDE.md sentence; it fails when either side changes alone.
guarded_text.mirror_of: Each `::selftest::` proof also names, in the manifest's `boundaries`, the CLI entry, tool or runtime default its claim describes, and invariant 60 fails when no live code in the pin's function calls that entry and the record states no gap naming it

guarded_text.text: **The independent pass runs BEFORE the claim is reported or merged**, not only at phase close. A universal claim that has not survived it is reported narrowed to what was actually tested, or not made.
guarded_text.why: A section 7.1 rule of docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md, outside the guarded corpus; deleting it fails invariant 60.

guarded_text.text: **A guard's denominator is DERIVED, never recalled.** Section 1 already says this about an audit's coverage sets; it binds a new guard's scan set too.
guarded_text.why: A section 7.1 rule of docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md, outside the guarded corpus; deleting it fails invariant 60.

guarded_text.text: **Remediation that touches the same guard earns a second pass.** A remediation can trade one defect for another, and a fix authored by the same reader who found the defect is not independently verified.
guarded_text.why: A section 7.1 rule of docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md, outside the guarded corpus; deleting it fails invariant 60.

guarded_text.text: **A pass reads one pinned commit.** Every agent in a pass reads the same commit and reports the SHA it read (`tools/tree_pin.py`); findings from agents that read different trees are not merged into one verdict.
guarded_text.why: A section 7.1 rule of docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md, outside the guarded corpus; deleting it fails invariant 60.

guarded_text.text: **A commit pushed before the pass returns states the mechanism changed, not the property.**
guarded_text.why: A section 7.1 rule of docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md, outside the guarded corpus; deleting it fails invariant 60.

guarded_text.text: **A pass is complete when its verification stage has returned.** A lens finding is REPORTED; only the refutation round moves it to VERIFIED or KILLED
guarded_text.why: A section 7.2 rule of docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md, outside the guarded corpus; deleting it fails invariant 60.

guarded_text.text: **A pass that could not run is DID NOT RUN, never clean.** A zero from a checker whose agents never executed is the same defect as a guard that scans nothing
guarded_text.why: A section 7.2 rule of docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md, outside the guarded corpus; deleting it fails invariant 60.

guarded_text.text: **The adversarial vectors are not chosen by the author.** Mutations the author picks confirm the fix the author meant
guarded_text.why: A section 7.2 rule of docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md, outside the guarded corpus; deleting it fails invariant 60.

guarded_text.text: **Report an involuntarily incomplete pass as incomplete.**
guarded_text.why: A section 7.2 rule of docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md, outside the guarded corpus; deleting it fails invariant 60.

guarded_text.text: **A claim-proof pin binds at the outermost boundary its claim describes**: the CLI entry, tool or default-resolution path a person hits, not the function the change touched.
guarded_text.why: A section 7.3 rule of docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md, outside the guarded corpus; deleting it fails invariant 60.

guarded_text.text: **Rule text outside the guarded corpus is recorded in the manifest.** Each bold-lead rule in this section 7, and each AGENTS.md sentence that restates a bound or exempted CLAUDE.md sentence, has a `guarded_text` record in `tools/claim-proof-manifest.json`.
guarded_text.why: A section 7.3 rule of docs/AUDIT-PROTOCOL.md, outside the guarded corpus; deleting it fails invariant 60.

_detector_branches_why: Recorded branch names for the two detectors that scan text. Fixture/branch agreement alone only catches a half delete; with the names recorded here, removing a branch AND its fixture in one edit still fails the build. A missing table, a missing key, or an entry that is not a non-empty list of names fails the check instead of skipping the pin.
